content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read_document on candidate_specs.md and any rate/latency/simulation guidance documents. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, assign them numeric IDs 1–3 for recording, and record the numeric constraints: threshold min/max, required minimum efficiency, maximum latency, allocated rate if stated, and each candidate latency."},{"id":"s2","description":"Filter the three candidates using the hard latency requirement latency <= 4.0 us and the candidate_specs.md eligibility rules. Record a numeric pass/fail flag for each candidate, and proceed only with latency-valid candidates."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every latency-valid candidate, run simulate_efficiency at a coarse threshold grid spanning 20–60 GeV, e.g. 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60 GeV. Record every numeric tuple: candidate ID, threshold, returned signal efficiency, and whether efficiency >= 80%."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best coarse-scan regions for each candidate, especially any points near the maximum efficiency and any points near the 80% requirement. Run simulate_efficiency on a finer grid, preferably 1 GeV spacing, around those regions while staying within 20–60 GeV. Record all numeric results."},{"id":"s5","description":"From all recorded simulations, select the valid candidate/threshold point with latency <= 4.0 us, threshold in 20–60 GeV, and efficiency >= 80% that has the highest signal efficiency at the allocated rate. Record the selected candidate ID, threshold, efficiency, and latency; if no point satisfies the hard constraints, record that no valid recommendation exists using numeric flags."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Algorithm-L2","threshold_gev":36,"justification":"Algorithm-L2 at 36 GeV is the best-performing physics choice in the completed threshold scan: it achieves the highest recorded signal efficiency, 93.212%, exceeding the 80% minimum and outperforming Algorithm-L1's best point of 86.907% and Algorithm-L3's best point of 75.623%. However, the recorded project results indicate that Level-1 FPGA latency is unstated/unknown for all three candidates, so no candidate is fully verified against the hard 4.0 us latency requirement.
